caspase 11 and caspases 1 and 5 differentially modulate cofilin phosphorylation via RhoA, Slingshot and LIMK, respectively, to promote actin polymerization and bacterial clearance.
caspase 11 and caspases 1 differentially modulated actin polymerization to promote bacterial clearance by phosphorylating or dephosphorylating cofilin, via RhoA or Slingshot proteins, respectively.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of actin dynamics and caspases in the intracellular trafficking of Legionella pneumophila.
the mechanisms by which the innate immune system controls intracellular pathogens.
the molecular basis of the inflammatory process, and how the immune system responds to infection with intracellular bacteria.

caspase 11 is required to phosphorylate cofilin to induce actin depolymerization, which promotes the fusion of Legionella-containing phagosomes with lysosomes.
caspase 1 and 11 have opposing roles in the actin cytoskeleton, which are critical for bacterial clearance.

caspase11 and caspases-1 have opposing effects on actin dynamics, and this impacts on the fusion of pathogenic bacteria-containing vacuoles to lysosomes.
